clue.text: Wickedness in half-sleazy city

indicators.note: the wickedness word is placed in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: the first half of the word sleazy

explanation.surface: A city that is only half as seedy as its reputation still hides some vice.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: Barbara Seville is one of the punning friends, after The Barber of Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is a large Spanish city, capital of Andalusia.

clue.text: Visual signals from angry holder of incorrect map, eh?

indicators.note: the angry word holds the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: sore means angry in American usage

indicators.note: the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a wrong map flags it with frantic gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is signaling with flags or arms, a visual code.

clue.text: Extremely curtailed happening contributes to eccentric term for a New England native

indicators.note: a curtailed word has its tail cut off
the happening word is put into the jumbled letters
eccentric means odd, so the letters go askew

explanation.surface: A cut-short event adds a quirky regional nickname for a Yankee.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the six New England states, and a Vermonter is someone from there.

clue.text: Without leadership, sadly, circling globe to arrive at Asian country

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the round letter
losing its leader drops the first letter

parts.note: O is round like a globe

explanation.surface: A leaderless, unhappy traveler circles the world to reach Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Selfish, dysfunctional cities taking turn

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the turn word inside them
something dysfunctional is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Self-centered, broken cities take their turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoistic describes someone concerned only with their own interests.

clue.text: Comedian Lee cut fool short

indicators.note: together with short, says the end of the word is lopped off
a word made short loses its last letter here

parts.note: a dupe is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A comedian named Lee interrupts a fool before he finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up is a comic who performs solo routines in front of a live audience.

clue.text: Flood planter containing hydrogen

indicators.note: the planter word holds the element symbol inside

explanation.surface: A gardener soaks the beds with hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: To shower is to flood or deluge, as in showering someone with gifts.

clue.text: Gash lent Mr. Wilder a safe distance

indicators.note: more wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone lends a cut to Gene Wilder, then keeps well away.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr. Wilder looks like a person; Wilder is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone at arm's length means keeping them at a cautious distance.

clue.text: Performer takes five in state capital

indicators.note: the performer word takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: a doer is someone who performs
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An actor grabs a five-minute break in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: Ben Dover is one of the punning friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the capital of Delaware.

clue.text: Partially atop an exquisite piece of glass

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of atop and the start of exquisite

explanation.surface: Something perched on top of an exquisite glass object.
explanation.definitionFit: A pane is a single sheet of glass in a window.

clue.text: Traveler to disfigure policeman near squalid loo

indicators.note: set beside, so the pieces follow one after another
something squalid is in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveler vandalizes a policeman standing beside a filthy toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant famous for his journey to China, the archetypal traveler.

clue.text: Nonconformist replacing Rick with neutral expert

indicators.note: names what is added in Rick's place, at the end
Rick is taken out of the nonconformist word to make room

parts.note: a maverick is an independent nonconformist

explanation.surface: A rebel loses someone called Rick and gains a neutral specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for neutral, as on an electrical plug or a gear lever.
explanation.definitionFit: A maven is a connoisseur or specialist, from Yiddish.

clue.text: Return ring where you play 9

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Come back to the ring where some game is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is MARCO POLO, the call-and-response tag game children play in a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo is a game played in a swimming pool, so the pool is its venue.

clue.text: Pennsylvania squad maneuvers around the French

indicators.note: the maneuvering word goes around the French article

parts.note: steers is maneuvers, as a verb

explanation.surface: A Pennsylvania team runs plays around some Frenchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pittsburgh Steelers are an American football team based in Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Insect and tailless arachnid taking bow at a cold location

indicators.note: the pieces line up, the arachnid taking the bow just before it

parts.note: an arc is a bow shape

indicators.note: without its tail, the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A bug and a stubby spider take a bow on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica, the southern polar continent, is the coldest place on Earth.

clue.text: Choosing to join a kind of art with endless trace of color (chic!)

parts.note: op art is a style of optical-illusion art

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tinge is a trace of color

explanation.surface: An art lover signs up for a style with just a hint of fashionable color.
explanation.definitionFit: Opting in means electing to take part, which is choosing to join.

clue.text: Singes metamorphic rock

indicators.note: metamorphic means changed in form, so the letters change their arrangement

parts.note: these six letters are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: Heat singes a rock until it turns metamorphic.
explanation.walkthrough: Metamorphic does double work: it signals the rearrangement and also describes the rock, since this rock is metamorphic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded rock formed by heat and pressure on older stone.

clue.text: Weirdly long title is acquired through deceitful methods

indicators.note: arranged in a weird way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An oddly long title was obtained by fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains are those obtained dishonestly.

clue.text: Rising American: one who pays for a means of support

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: An upwardly mobile American bankrolls a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US, suspenders hold up trousers; in Britain they hold up stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender holds up clothing, so it is a means of support.

clue.text: British politician involved in winter sport is pinching pennies

indicators.note: the politician is set inside the sport word

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A British politician on a ski holiday is economizing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimping means being stingy, spending as little as possible.

clue.text: If work is delayed, model tool becomes something that could block a canal

definitions.text: something that could block a canal

indicators.note: work is the physics symbol, and delaying it moves that leading letter of the model word to its back

parts.note: to model clothes is to wear them
ax is the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: A model tool, held up long enough, turns into a canal obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the ear canal, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwax builds up in the ear canal and can plug it.

clue.text: Bowling? Let's cut loose and play to begin with

indicators.note: the play word comes first in the answer, ahead of the jumbled letters

parts.note: a skit is a short comic play

indicators.note: letters cut loose are freed to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bowling night: everyone lets go and plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is the British name for a form of ninepin bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is a game of knocking down pins with a ball, a kind of bowling.

clue.text: In tub, note a sign of life

indicators.note: the note goes into the tub word

parts.note: re is a note of the scale

explanation.surface: Humming a note in the bathtub shows someone is alive.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: Xavier Breath is one of the punning friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing is a basic indicator that someone is alive.

clue.text: Perform on the guitar, keeping muscle in range

indicators.note: the guitar word keeps the muscle inside it

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A guitarist who stays in shape while practicing scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a whole range, as in the spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Take steps to secure a bit of eternal rest

indicators.note: the steps word secures the small piece inside it

parts.note: to pace is to take steps

indicators.note: only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Walking about to guarantee some eternal repose.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: Warren Peace is one of the punning friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is calm and quiet, as in rest in peace.

clue.text: Goren's first ace vanished

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the bridge player's name is used

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Charles Goren, the bridge expert, finds his leading ace has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone is a synonym for vanished: no longer present.

clue.text: Container is a lawyer's concern

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a box or holder
second meaning: a legal action a lawyer handles

explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: Justin Case is one of the punning friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a box for holding things and a lawsuit before a court.

clue.text: Conclusions of sudoku, Ken-Ken, and kakuro in reverse

indicators.note: the final letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the puzzle name counts as one word, so only its final letter

explanation.surface: Finishing logic puzzles in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to reverse it, as with the undo button.

clue.text: A pitch I assembled for old video-game machine

indicators.note: the pieces are put together one after another

parts.note: tar and pitch are both black sticky substances

explanation.surface: A sales pitch I put together for a retro games console.
explanation.definitionFit: Atari made the 2600, one of the first home video-game consoles.

clue.text: Antagonized a particular contrarian, claiming a little space

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the little space
a contrarian goes the opposite way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: an en is a small printer's space

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed a particular naysayer who grabbed a bit of room.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them hostile, which is to antagonize them.

clue.text: Base of a log and two trees? Nonsense

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
yew and ash are both trees

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a log and two trees that turns out to be rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Base of a log suggests the bottom of a piece of wood; it is the mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is talk meant to deceive, humbug or nonsense.

clue.text: Orange mixed with red is what you'll find repeatedly among Lois Carmen Denominator's friends Anita, Barbara, Ben, Jean, Justin, Ophelia, Polly, Warren, and Xavier, whose last names are answers to the italicized clues

definitions.text: what you'll find repeatedly among Lois Carmen Denominator's friends Anita, Barbara, Ben, Jean, Justin, Ophelia, Polly, Warren, and Xavier, whose last names are answers to the italicized clues

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order

parts.note: R is the color code for red

explanation.surface: A paint recipe, then a joke cast list of friends with punning names.
explanation.walkthrough: Lois Carmen Denominator puns on lowest common denominator; the friends include Barbara Seville, Ben Dover, Jean Pool, Justin Case, Warren Peace and Xavier Breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A groaner is a pun so bad it makes people groan, and every friend's name is one.
